requirements.summary: Baseline showed root:root ownership (cmd-72318c31c4d84e70, cmd-be56bbed04c34d4f). Executor created the inventorysvc system user and ran chown -R inventorysvc:inventory-readers (cmd-bde701fceea24e27, cmd-13da4cf3864f4a17), directly verified via ls -lad output showing inventorysvc as owner. Ownership persisted after a full reboot (cmd-9a0babb24dec4832).

Directories set to 750 and files to 640 with group inventory-readers (cmd-13da4cf3864f4a17). Directly tested: a temporary user added to inventory-readers (reader_test) successfully read records.csv (exit 0) in cmd-c65e5781c6854f62. Group and permissions confirmed intact post-restart (cmd-9a0babb24dec4832).

A temporary unrelated test user (other_test, no group membership) was directly denied read access (exit 1, 'Permission denied') in cmd-c65e5781c6854f62, confirming the 750/640 mode with no world access is effective.

cat output of records.csv and config.json immediately after the permission change (cmd-13da4cf3864f4a17) matches the content implied by the prepared baseline, and md5sum checks before and after the reboot are identical (cmd-b36b86c972bc4ccd vs cmd-9a0babb24dec4832), confirming no content drift from the ownership/permission repair or the restart.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on node1
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baseline captured boot_id bef0e5ec... with healthy permissions/checksums (cmd-b36b86c972bc4ccd). Reboot acknowledged via systemd-run (cmd-797755e6ebcf430b). Connection loss during the reboot window (cmd-4f8ab05da57d4ca6, cmd-135f6e5ecb884b7a, cmd-df8aab0309dd4350) followed by reconnection with a new boot_id 3972bbb0... (cmd-1788c9b867a740f7), cross-checked against the fixed global boot-identity snapshots (global:after_prepare boot-identity bef0e5ec... vs global:after_executor boot-identity 3972bbb0...). Post-restart recovery of ownership, permissions, checksums, and accounts confirmed (cmd-9a0babb24dec4832).

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task — ownership by inventorysvc, group-read access for inventory-readers, denial of access to other users, and preservation of existing content — are directly demonstrated with before/after evidence, including survival across a full node reboot with boot-identity change confirmed both in the executor trace and the fixed lifecycle snapshots. The mandatory node-restart evidence protocol was also fully and coherently captured for node1.
limitations: Content preservation is corroborated via matching md5sum before/after the reboot and matching cat output at the time of the permission change, but the executor did not directly recompute the sha256 hashes recorded in the prepare-stage baseline for a byte-for-byte cryptographic comparison.

operational_hygiene.summary: The executor created two temporary test accounts (reader_test, other_test) solely to validate the access-control requirement (cmd-c65e5781c6854f62) — a bounded, low-risk, task-relevant mutation. Initial cleanup attempts (cmd-e4a5c0da3d6a4907, cmd-dfefe0d6a4744f82) failed because lingering systemd --user sessions for those accounts blocked userdel; the executor escalated with loginctl terminate-user and a final userdel (cmd-15284d654bbf4078), fully removing both accounts before the reboot. Final state (cmd-9a0babb24dec4832) and the after_executor lifecycle snapshot confirm no residue from the test accounts. No unnecessary or unreverted mutations were found; the extra cleanup commands were corrective follow-through on the same bounded test rather than a new unnecessary mutation.
